subject: Observability egress: secure forwarding (Splunk HEC / syslog) + fallback routing Q&A
conversation_summary: Planning and Q&A for secure log/metric export from a VPC/on‑prem Redwood Private deployment to customer SIEM (Splunk HEC + syslog). Topics: mTLS tunnel and client certs, NAT/egress IP allowlisting, fallback to hosted endpoints, token rotation and retention, tracing span headers and sampling, acceptance testing and canary timeline.
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.example.com>
To: SecureOps Inc <ops@secureops.example.com>; Splunk Onboarding <onboard@splunk.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.example.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability egress — initial diagram and questions

Hi team,

Attaching a first-pass diagram for how Redwood Private (VPC-hosted) would forward telemetry to your SIEM stack for NimbleBank. High-level:

- Metrics -> Prometheus remote_write to an internal aggregator, pushed to your Ingest via an mTLS HEC proxy.
- Logs -> fluentd forwarder (syslog-ng compatible) over TLS to a collector cluster in your VPC.
- Traces -> OTLP over gRPC, sampling decisions made locally with a 10% baseline and trace hooks to attach request-id/span-context headers.

Open questions we need your input on:
1) Do you require client certificate authentication (mutual TLS) for HEC or is TLS+API-token sufficient?
2) For egress allowlisting — do you need a single static IP per site, or are CIDR blocks acceptable?
3) Fallback behavior: if your endpoint is unreachable, can we buffer and retry for up to 48 hours, or do you require a drop-path plus a call-home to Redwood?

Attachments: obs-egress-diagram-v1.png, siem-requirements-202608.docx

Next steps: Naomi and I will collect your answers and update the handshake checklist. Can we sync by EOD?

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.example.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.example.com>
Cc: SecureOps Inc <ops@secureops.example.com>, Splunk Onboarding <onboard@splunk.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability egress — initial diagram and questions

Diego / team,

Couple of clarifications from the Redwood side after reviewing the diagram and requirements doc:

- HEC: We strongly prefer mTLS with client certs for Splunk HEC when transmitting production logs (PII/transactional). Token-only can be an interim option for POC but will require explicit exception for retention/attestation.
- NAT / IPs: For customer-managed on-prem we can support either static egress IP (recommended) or a small CIDR range. For managed VPC deployments we can publish an egress set but it's typically a /29 or /28.
- Buffering / Drop policy: Our forwarder supports durable disk buffering (configurable up to 72h) and exponential backoff. We can also implement a controlled drop with an audit log entry if you prefer guaranteed drop semantics beyond 48h.
- Tracing: We will emit a X-Redwood-Trace header and preserve upstream traceparent/span-context; please confirm the header you will accept for end-to-end stitching (we propose `traceparent`).

Action items I can own:
- Produce an mTLS deployment checklist for the customer (cert issuance, rotation cadence, CA pinning).
- Add a short acceptance-test plan for verifying span continuity and sample logs.

Diego — I added a small note in the diagram where we need the exact CIDR or IP.

- Naomi

Naomi Feldman
Product Security | Redwood Inference
From: SecureOps Inc <ops@secureops.example.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.example.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Splunk Onboarding <onboard@splunk.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability egress — initial diagram and questions

Hi Diego / Naomi,

Thanks for the diagram and notes. Quick answers from the Ops side at NimbleBank:

- We mandate client cert mTLS for any stream carrying logs with account identifiers. Token-only endpoints are allowed for metrics (prometheus) but HEC must be mTLS.
- We can provide either a static NAT IP per datacenter (preferred) or a /29 for VPC peers. Please include both options in the checklist.
- Buffer policy: 48h buffer is acceptable; beyond that we need an alert and a manual review step.

Two tactical questions before we proceed:
1) For the Splunk HEC topology — can Redwood terminate TLS on a forwarder inside the customer's VPC (i.e., run a lightweight proxy) instead of connecting directly from customer infra to Splunk SaaS? This reduces NAT surface for us.
2) In case of full-site outage, would Redwood allow a temporary fallback to Redwood-hosted ingest (hosted API) under a signed SLA and tokenized envelope? We'd need clear data residency and E2E encryption assurances.

We can schedule a short call tomorrow afternoon.

— Aaron (ops@nimblebank.com)
SecureOps Inc (on behalf of NimbleBank)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.example.com>
To: SecureOps Inc <ops@secureops.example.com>, Splunk Onboarding <onboard@splunk.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.example.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability egress — initial diagram and questions

Aaron / team,

Thanks — answers inline and next steps: 

1) mTLS termination proxy: Yes. We can deploy a small forwarder/proxy (Redwood forwarder) inside the customer's VPC that terminates incoming telemetry and re-encrypts it to your SIEM. That forwarder can be pinned to a single egress IP and controlled via a small terraform module.

2) Fallback to Redwood-hosted ingest: We can support a temporary, contract-managed failover where data is forwarded to a Redwood-hosted, customer-dedicated ingest endpoint. Constraints: data-at-rest will be encrypted with a customer-managed key (KMS) and access logs will be delivered to the customer's audit bucket. We will prepare a short addendum to the SLA that lists retention and encryption guarantees.

Action items / timeline: 
- Naomi: mTLS checklist and cert rotation cadence (deliverable: 2026-08-24).
- Diego: prepare terraform snippet for forwarder + sample NAT mapping and send handshake-checklist.csv (deliverable: 2026-08-25).
- Kimberly: capture SOC2 evidence requirements and a short statement for the contract addendum (cc'd).

Please confirm a 30-minute sync tomorrow 14:00 ET / 11:00 PT. If that works we'll walk through the diagram and the canary plan.

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: handshake-checklist.csv
